newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Slower advertising growth hits SPH's shares.
newsitem.headline: Slower advertising growth hits SPH's shares.

text.p: Shares in government-linked newspaper and publications group Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) are being pushed down as investors anticipate lacklustre advertising growth, analysts said on Monday.

SPH's foreign shares dropped from S$27.90 (US$20) in late June to S$23.80 in mid August. On Monday, SPH's foreign shares were hovering around S$24.40. Analysts normally track SPH's foreign shares as its local tranche is considered illiquid.
"SPH's share price has been falling in anticipation that advertising revenue numbers will be weak," said Michael Ong, an analyst at Crosby Securities.
The company, which controls all of Singapore's daily newspapers in all languages, completed its financial year on August 31 and is expected to report its results in October or November.

Analysts predict SPH's advertising revenues will rise between 8.0 and 10 percent. Although this is not far off the 10 percent rise in the previous financial year, analysts say 1995/96 growth would be boosted by an advertising rate rise in January.
What was more significant was that advertising volume growth was likely to be flat, they said.
Analysts said advertising volume growth had shrunk from 16 percent in 1993/94 to 6.0 percent in 1994/95 and would probably be flat in 1995/96.
Among the factors weighing on advertising volume was the rash of measures introduced by the government in May to curb property speculation.
"It is widely acknowledged that the move has dampened ads for property sales," said an analyst at a foreign broking house.
Analysts said although SPH could get some relief from softening newsprint prices in 1997, advertising revenue was the key concern.
"Advertising revenue is everything to them. About 75 percent of their turnover depends on advertising," said the foreign firm's analyst.
Advertising revenue growth is not expected to get much lift into 1997-1998 either.
"I don't think advertising revenue will pick up. It is likely to be single digit," said Michael Sia, analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Sia predicted advertising revenue growth of 5.0 percent for 1996/97 and 6.0 percent for 1997/98.
Analysts said another rise in advertising rates could be counter-productive as advertisers were unlikely to have bigger budgets and would simply spend the same amount on fewer advertisements.
The cloudy outlook for advertising revenue would continue to put a lid on the SPH share price as other areas of business would not make significant contributions until possibly 1998, they said.
"I think the shares will stay between S$22-24 in the near term," said Ong. ($1 = S$1.40)
